# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 3
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 3

---

1. And when the Lord had thus spoken, I fell upon my face and wept, and I said: "O Lord, according to what you have said, is it possible that a man who commits sin should then repent and be saved? And what of those who die in their sin?"

2. And the Lord answered me: "The sinners shall repent when they see those who are believed in. So also, those who did not believe shall see those who believed, and shall be ashamed of their unbelief."

3. "And those who repent shall be saved, and they shall dwell with the righteous in the glory of my Father. But those who continue in their sin shall be judged and condemned to punishment according to their deeds."

4. And I said: "O Lord, allow me to see what becomes of the souls of the sinners and the righteous at the time of their departure from this world."

5. And the Lord showed me a great angel, terrible in aspect, who held in his right hand a fiery sword, and fire poured from his body.

6. And there were beside him two other angels, and above them another, more bright and glorious, and these were they who had charge of the souls of the sinners.

7. And the other angels were luminous and clothed in light, and they received the souls of the righteous, who praised God with a great voice.

8. And the angel of righteousness brought forward the souls of the righteous, and brought them near to me, and I saw their faces shining as the sun.

9. And I said to the Lord: "Who are these?"

10. And the Lord said to me: "These are your brothers, the righteous, whose works you do not yet know. But they are known to me."

11. And I asked: "What of the sinners, Lord? Where are they taken?"

12. And the Lord answered me: "The sinners are taken by the angel who presides over the punishments, and they are led to the place of punishment."

---
*EMET note: Chapter 3 is primarily from the Ethiopic recension; the Akhmim fragment does not preserve this section fully. The transition to the hell-tour begins here.*
